deadlock_regression_real: confirmed (>64KiB real ANSI, real path, reproduces). The test spawns a real fake_claude child (--query-burst 200KiB) whose burst is scrollback filler interleaved with the exact three real query sequences the racefix handlers answer (DA1 \x1b[c, DA2 \x1b[>c, CPR \x1b[6n) every 25 lines; Daemon A produces it as live output, a second independently-constructed Daemon B reattaches to A's still-live real ptyhost via ATTACH(-1) and receives the entire 210KB query-heavy burst as its replay, feeding it through the real emulator.Feed. This is the exact production deadlock path (Feed of a survivor replay containing queries with no drainer running). Ring-length (>=200KiB) and same-pid reattach are both asserted, so the test cannot pass via a fresh spawn / empty replay / toy data. Self-report's revert-and-hang reproduction (45s timeout + goroutine dump matching the reported io.pipe.write<-DA-handler<-Feed<-EnsureStarted-spawnMu stack) is credible and consistent with the code; I did not re-perform the destructive stash-revert but confirmed the pass side and the 45s deadlock-detecting bound in the test.
discard_forward_correct: sound (no live dropped / no historical forwarded in practice). Direction that matters for the reviewer's stated fear (a dropped LIVE response = a NEW hang) is impossible: replayFed is closed before the live readLoop goroutine starts, so any live query response is generated only after forwarding has (or will immediately) latch true — live responses are always forwarded, never discarded. Unbuffered-pipe reasoning for the discard side is correct: Feed(replay) cannot return until every replay-era response byte has been Read by the drainer, so all historical responses are consumed while forwarding is still false. MINOR (non-blocking) edge: there is a theoretical scheduling window where the drainer could classify the FINAL replay response chunk AFTER close(replayFed) and thus forward it; this is benign (a duplicate DA/CPR response byte-sequence to claude's stdin, which claude ignores as unsolicited input — not a hang) and effectively unreachable with realistic data (real replays, and this test's burst, end in rendered screen content well past the last query, so Feed keeps parsing filler after the last response is read+classified, leaving close(replayFed) well after). Not a correctness defect.
discovery_barrier_correct: both GC gated, armed pre-Run, released on failure, serve unblocked. gcTuiOrphans AND gcAgentOrphans both return early on !discoveryGateOpen(); ArmDiscoveryBarrier is called before st.Run and installs discoveryDone (written once pre-Run, read only from the scan goroutine — store -race -count=2 clean, confirms no race on the unlocked field); release is a deferred call inside the single discovery goroutine so it fires on both success and every error/return path; runDiscoveryAsync is a bare `go fn()` so ListenAndServe is never blocked (proven by TestRunDiscoveryAsyncDoesNotBlockCaller with a never-returning fn). A permanently wedged discovery keeps GC deferred forever — this is the intended SAFE direction (orphan GC is a cleanup nicety; lazy first-WS-attach still re-adopts), and it cannot wedge serve. Single barrier over ALL (sequential tui-then-agent) discovery correctly handles the shared run-dir/seed-space so neither GC pass can race the other manager's in-flight adoption.
